sections.name: File setup
sections.title: The whole web page
sections.what: The single page that holds the app's title, description, icon, empty root container, and the main script that starts the app.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the standard entry page for a single-page app.
sections.watch_out: The body classes here may override the body rule in index.css, so colors changed in the stylesheet may not show.

summary: The single web page that loads the app: it sets the title, description, icon, the empty root element, and loads the main script.
purpose: The first page the browser opens.
why: Standard setup for a Vite app. The title and description show in browser tabs and search previews.
how: It sets the text encoding and the mobile screen width, links the icon, sets the title and description, adds an empty root element for React, sets the body classes, and loads the main script.
inputs: The icon file, the main script, and the root element.
outputs: The page the browser shows, which React fills with the app.
risks: The body classes set a very dark background and light text. These classes likely take priority over the body rule in index.css, so the page may look dark even though the stylesheet asks for light grey.
debug: If the page is blank, check the root element's name and the script path. If the page colors are wrong, compare the body classes here with the body rule in index.css.
